$comment: The registry of every diagnostic code pkinative reports. The diagnostics-parity rule of scripts/verify-docs.ts keeps it in bidirectional sync with the PkiDiagnosticCode union of src/types/pki-types.ts and requires a payload factory for every code in src/core/pki-diagnostics.ts. The union is additions-only: a code is never renamed or removed. Delivery: strict: true throws PKI_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC; onDiagnostic receives every diagnostic; otherwise console.warn once per code per operation. Parse results also record every diagnostic.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A serial number is longer than 20 octets.
diagnostics.remedy: Accept or refuse by policy; some verifiers refuse such certificates.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A serial number is zero or negative.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still returned as decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The outer signatureAlgorithm differs from tbsCertificate.signature.
diagnostics.remedy: Treat the certificate as unverifiable; a verifier must refuse it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 algorithm identifier has absent or non-NULL parameters.
diagnostics.remedy: Accept or refuse by policy; RFC 3279 requires NULL parameters.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A certificate carries extensions but declares version 1 or 2.
diagnostics.remedy: The extensions are still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A certificate carries a unique identifier but declares version 1.
diagnostics.remedy: The identifier is still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A validity date before 2050 is encoded as a GeneralizedTime.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is decoded correctly; the issuer violates the RFC 5280 encoding rule.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A GeneralizedTime in a certificate carries fractional seconds.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is decoded to the millisecond; RFC 5280 forbids fractions in certificates.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: notBefore is later than notAfter.
diagnostics.remedy: The certificate is valid at no instant; refuse it wherever validity matters.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The issuer name is an empty sequence.
diagnostics.remedy: Chain building by name will not find an issuer; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The subject is empty and subjectAltName is absent or not critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Read the identity from subjectAltName, and treat the certificate as non-conforming.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A subjectAltName or issuerAltName extension contains no GeneralName.
diagnostics.remedy: The extension carries no identity; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A multi-valued relative distinguished name is not in DER SET OF order.
diagnostics.remedy: Compare names attribute by attribute, never by bytes.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A PrintableString contains an ASCII character outside the PrintableString alphabet, such as '*', '@' or '&'.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ASCII; web PKI issuers commonly do this in wildcard names.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A TeletexString is decoded.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ISO 8859-1, the interpretation of real-world issuers; read the raw bytes when T.61 semantics matter.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A critical extension has an OID pkinative does not decode.
diagnostics.remedy: A verifier must refuse the certificate unless it processes the extension itself (the raw value is kept).

diagnostics.raisedWhen: basicConstraints sets pathLenConstraint while cA is false.
diagnostics.remedy: Ignore the constraint; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: keyUsage asserts no bit.
diagnostics.remedy: Treat the key as usable for nothing; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A named bit list, such as keyUsage, keeps trailing zero bits.
diagnostics.remedy: The bits decode identically; the encoder is not DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: nameConstraints is not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Enforce the constraints anyway; RFC 5280 requires conforming CAs to mark them critical.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: nameConstraints appears in a certificate whose basicConstraints does not assert cA.
diagnostics.remedy: Ignore the constraints: the extension MUST be used only in a CA certificate, and an end-entity certificate issues nothing for it to constrain. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: basicConstraints asserts cA without being marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative reads the extension whatever its criticality, which is the safe direction; a verifier that skipped non-critical extensions would not see that this is a CA. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: policyConstraints is present and not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative enforces it anyway; a verifier that ignored it would grant a path the policy the CA withheld. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: keyUsage asserts keyCertSign while basicConstraints does not assert cA.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing to do: RFC 5280 §6.1.4 (k) refuses to let a certificate without cA issue anything, whatever its keyUsage says. The bit is for CA certificates only and the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A v3 certificate that names another subject as its issuer carries no authorityKeyIdentifier.
diagnostics.remedy: Build the path by issuer name instead, trying every candidate whose subject matches: buildCertificatePath already does, so this costs exploration rather than correctness. When you are the issuer, computeKeyIdentifier over your own key bits and encodeAuthorityKeyIdentifier write it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A v3 certificate asserting cA carries no subjectKeyIdentifier.
diagnostics.remedy: Certificates this CA issues cannot name its key, so their authorityKeyIdentifier will match nothing and path building falls back to names. computeKeyIdentifier over the CA public key bits and encodeSubjectKeyIdentifier write it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The subject carries a commonName that is not one of the subjectAltName entries, and the certificate has a subjectAltName.
diagnostics.remedy: Match the host against subjectAltName only, which is what checkServerName does whenever a SAN names a host. A name appearing only in the commonName is one no modern relying party will match, and CA/Browser Forum BR 7.1.4.3 forbids issuing it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A dNSName in subjectAltName or issuerAltName falls outside RFC 1034's preferred name syntax — an empty label, a leading or trailing dot, or a character outside letters, digits and hyphen.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is compared literally, so it can only ever match a host asked for with the same spelling; nothing silently normalises it. Underscores are common in practice and resolve in DNS, which is why this is a diagnostic and not a refusal.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: authorityKeyIdentifier carries only one of authorityCertIssuer and authorityCertSerialNumber.
diagnostics.remedy: Use keyIdentifier for chain building; the pair is unusable alone.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: certificatePolicies lists one policy OID more than once.
diagnostics.remedy: Every occurrence is kept as decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: policyConstraints sets neither requireExplicitPolicy nor inhibitPolicyMapping.
diagnostics.remedy: The extension constrains nothing; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A field with a DEFAULT value carries that value explicitly: version v1, critical FALSE, cA FALSE, a subtree minimum of 0.
diagnostics.remedy: Every reader decodes the same value, so the certificate is read as encoded (as Go, OpenSSL and BoringSSL read it); pass strict: true to refuse encoders that are not DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: encodingRules is 'ber' and the input uses a construct DER forbids (indefinite length, constructed string, non-minimal length, a non-canonical BOOLEAN).
diagnostics.remedy: Expected for BER inputs such as CMS; never re-sign or compare such bytes as if they were DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: mode is 'lax' and a block deviates from the strict grammar: whitespace around a boundary line or inside the base64 text, base64 lines that are not 64 characters long, or RFC 1421 headers. Explanatory text outside blocks is ignored in both modes, as RFC 7468 §2 requires.
diagnostics.remedy: Expected for hand-edited or legacy PEM; fix the producer to get strict output.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A SignedData or SignerInfo declares a version RFC 5652 defines, but not the one §5.1 or §5.3 derives from what it carries — for instance a SignedData declaring 1 while a signer uses subjectKeyIdentifier, which calls for 3.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing to do as a verifier: the version is not signed and decides nothing, and RFC 5652 §1.3 asks readers to be forgiving of it. Report it to the producer, since a strict reader may refuse the message.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: One of the SET OF fields that no signature covers — digestAlgorithms, certificates, crls or signerInfos — is not in DER order (X.690 §11.6). Common: 91 of the 224 signed messages in NIST PKITS carry an unsorted certificate set.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing signed depends on the order, so verification is unaffected. Report it to the producer if the message must pass a strict DER reader.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A signer's signed attributes are not in DER SET OF order, which RFC 5652 §5.3 requires. The signature is verified over the bytes as they were signed, not over a re-sorted set.
diagnostics.remedy: The signature may be perfectly good. Expect other verifiers — those that re-encode the set before checking the signature — to reject it, and report it to the producer.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A signer uses a digest algorithm that SignedData.digestAlgorithms does not list. The list lets a one-pass verifier start hashing the content before it reaches the signers.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative is not a one-pass verifier and is unaffected. RFC 5652 §5.1 lets such a verifier fail the message, so report it to the producer.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A PBKDF2 iteration count, for a key, a bag of certificates or a PBMAC1 MAC, is below the 1 000 RFC 8018 recommends. The file still opens.
diagnostics.remedy: The count sets what a stolen copy of the file costs to brute-force. Re-export it with a higher one — OpenSSL 3 writes 2 048 by default, and OWASP recommends 600 000 for PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA-256.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A CRL's cRLNumber or deltaCRLIndicator is not a DER INTEGER, or an entry's reasonCode is not a CRLReason value RFC 5280 assigns or its invalidityDate is not a GeneralizedTime. The value is ignored: none of them decides whether a serial is revoked, and a delta whose base number cannot be read is never paired with a base.
diagnostics.remedy: Report it to the CA that issued the list. A revocation with an unreadable reason is still a revocation; a delta with an unreadable base number answers nothing until the CA reissues it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A name attribute RFC 5280 Appendix A.1 defines is encoded outside its syntax: countryName, serialNumber or dnQualifier not a PrintableString, domainComponent or emailAddress not an IA5String, or a DirectoryString attribute (commonName, organizationName, …) as none of TeletexString, PrintableString, UniversalString, UTF8String and BMPString.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still decoded and names still compare by their bytes; a strict reader (pkilint, zlint) refuses the name, so have the issuer re-encode it — pkinative's encodeNameAttribute writes the defined type by default.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A countryName value is not exactly two characters (X520countryName ::= PrintableString (SIZE (2))).
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still decoded; the issuer should write the ISO 3166 alpha-2 code. encodeNameAttribute refuses any other length.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A BMPString or UniversalString starts with the byte-order signature U+FEFF (X.690: "Signatures shall not be used").
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded with the U+FEFF kept, so it compares unequal to the same text without it; the issuer should drop the signature.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A UTF8String, BMPString or UniversalString contains an ISO/IEC 2022 code-extension control (ESC, SO, SI, SS2 or SS3), which X.690 forbids in the ISO/IEC 10646 string types.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ISO/IEC 10646 regardless; a reader that honours the escape shows other characters, so treat the text with suspicion and have the issuer re-encode it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A subjectDirectoryAttributes extension is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The attributes are still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.
